Kuvitus: talvinen suomalainen maisema. P: Illustration: a winter landscape in Finland. A red detached house is drawn in cross-section: there is snow on the roof, smoke rises from the chimney and the house has a cellar below it. Underground is a layer of sandy soil and deeper down grey granite bedrock. An aeroplane flies in the sky, and far away behind the forest the reactor building of a nuclear power plant can be seen.
Vaakapylväskuvio mittakaavassa: suomalai: Horizontal bar chart to scale: the average effective dose of a Finn per year by source, STUK's estimate of the situation in 2018, about 5.9 millisieverts in total. Indoor radon about 4, other natural radiation, that is soil, buildings, space and the body's own substances, about 1.1 in total, and health care about 0.8 millisieverts per year. The bar of radon is clearly the longest, more than three times as long as the next one.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kaksi saman: Schematic figure, not to scale: two identical pieces of tissue. Gamma radiation enters the left one: a wavy line passes through the piece, and a few ionisation points lie sparsely along it. An alpha particle hits the right one: its short thick track stops inside the piece, and the ionisations along the track are dense. In both the absorbed dose is D = 1 milligray. The weighting factor of gamma radiation is 1, so the equivalent dose is 1 millisievert; the weighting factor of alpha radiation is 20, so the equivalent dose is 20 millisieverts.
Kaavakuva etäisyyden neliölaista. Vasemm: Schematic figure of the inverse-square law. On the left is a point source of radiation, from which four boundary rays spread to the right. At distance r the rays pass through one square; at distance 2 r the same radiation has to be spread over 2 times 2, that is four, squares of the same size, and at distance 3 r over 3 times 3, that is nine, squares. So one square receives a quarter of the radiation at distance 2 r and a ninth at distance 3 r, and the relative dose rate at these distances is 1, a quarter and a ninth.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: annosnopeus mikro: Graph to scale: dose rate in microsieverts per hour as a function of the thickness of a lead plate, thickness from zero to 30 millimetres. Without lead the dose rate is 40, and every 6 millimetre layer halves it: 20 at 6 millimetres, 10 at 12 millimetres, 5 at 18 millimetres. The curve falls ever more gently and never reaches zero. The half-value thickness is marked with a horizontal bracket at the first layer.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: gammasäteilyn ann: Graph to scale: dose rate of gamma radiation in microsieverts per hour as a function of the thickness of a concrete wall, thickness from zero to 25 centimetres, grid spacing 1 centimetre and 5 microsieverts per hour, every fifth vertical line and every second horizontal line darker; on the horizontal axis numbers at intervals of 5 centimetres and on the vertical axis at intervals of 10 microsieverts. Without concrete the dose rate is 80, and the curve falls ever more gently.
